title: Prove a sharp 1/4 error floor for contractive P104 mode deletion (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Prove a sharp **1/4 maximum coefficient-error floor** for contractive rank-seven approximation of the P104 Gram channel. This is a scoped obstruction with exact finite witnesses, without a new kappa or physical supplier.

```text
K = R R^T / 2
K_D = R D R^T / 2, D real symmetric, 0 <= D <= I, rank D <= 7
min_D max_ij |K_ij - (K_D)_ij| = 1/4
```

Every omitted half-spin root q gives an attaining dyadic projector `D=I-qq^T/2`. The lower bound uses only the retained D8 roots and covers every admissible real D. For some input `B e_i`, the output bias is at least `|B|/4`, so increasing arithmetic precision alone cannot make this mode deletion harmless.

The proof and verifier were produced by Nick Petalas. Credit Matarener's PR6166 for the P104 D8 coordinate identification and omitted-root signs, cited without re-verification; Rohan Arun PR1972, Chafik Boukhalfa PR1991 and their retained root/frame/native lineage for the Gram channel. All P104/helper/compiler/BIT predecessor credit is retained. Root geometry, projection and positive-semidefinite order are classical; no literature-wide novelty claim is made.

## Evidence

The exact finite replay checks sixteen new rank-seven projectors, all 173,056 entries of their error matrices, 6,560 nonzero integer-direction fixtures and three rejecting controls. A changed-receipt control also rejects under optimized Python. The written proof supplies the all-real-D quantifier.

Normal and optimized warning-strict checks and both registered VERIFY commands pass locally. The individually timed commands take about 0.17 seconds each, below their 120-second limits. Environment: CPython 3.12.15, macOS 27.0.1, arm64; standard library only. Syntax inspection, package metadata/pins, exact committed bytes and source-history preflight pass. Official export integrity and a Git-free, read-only optimized replay pass; all nine exported files retain their bytes and modes.

From the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/p104-contractive-gram-deflation/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -O -B research/p104-contractive-gram-deflation/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p104-contractive-gram-deflation
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/p104-contractive-gram-deflation --check-source-history
```

Expected markers: `PASS_P104_CONTRACTIVE_GRAM_DEFLATION`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`, `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`. A clean CPython 3.12 may replace the local interpreter path. RESULT.json is generated and binds all seven proof/input/metadata files.

Canonical main is `3f0152a32eeebac0df11946dbd50cabe5a7f7839`, priority revision 8. The coverage-law-change card explicitly changes to an original approximate-decoder question. The external coordinate identification is pinned by PR6166 head `096938513138868f0ed27639061f1a5054900f96` and path in MISSING.json; its factual signs are retained locally. The generic source-history pass covers declared canonical provenance, not scientific validation or ancestry of that external head. No pending Git object is needed for replay.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

This only covers real symmetric positive contractive filters and maximum entry error on the complete Gram block. Unrestricted rank-seven matrices, noncontractive/nonsymmetric filters, masked accuracy, changed side corrections, source encodings and nonlinear consumers remain open. A different word could correct the residual. No native, dirty-restoration, physical caller, full signed invoice, precision/tape, compiler, BIT, outer, Lean or selected cold replay is supplied. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. The selected frontier is unchanged.

## Open next questions

- Can an exact noncontractive or nonsymmetric rank-seven factor beat 1/4? Start with rational factors and certify every error entry; physical realization remains a separate obligation.
- Can a changed side correction absorb the explicit rank-one residual with a winning complete invoice? Start from one omitted-root projector and an actual scalar word.

## Related open work

- #6181 studies the complete P104 Gram stages under a common Gaussian-dyadic invertible code, including joint-bank mixing and restored scratch. Its endpoint correction-rank obstruction differs from this real contractive rank-seven coefficient-error floor; no common numerical optimum is computed.
- #6178 bounds exact decoder costs for functional binary pairings. Its support and lift hypotheses differ from this positive contractive approximation model; no decoder-cost optimum is computed here.
- #6166 supplies the cited P104 coordinates and studies ternary code uniqueness. This studies real contractive approximation and does not replay its code certificate.
- #6173 uses the same cited PR6166 root code and computes joint support 72 over F3 and Q. This theorem concerns real contractive Gram approximation and computes no competing support invariant.
- #6144 changes owned-register relay descent. This changes no word, lifetime or paid profile.
- #6167 retains an operand to remove a root stop. This supplies no competing complete kappa computation and does not exclude that changed word.
- #6169 resynthesizes scalar events while keeping the invoice. This concerns mathematical Gram approximation with its residual explicit.
- #6170 supplies P104 design and pricing tools. This standalone certificate invokes no word optimizer or legality oracle.
- #6171 reduces tensor frames under fixed boundaries. This is a real coefficient-error problem, with no tensor-moment optimum claimed.
- #6172 studies variable productive-boundary signed moments. This introduces no variable productive targets or negative credits.
- #6175 localizes ADD coefficient faults. This deliberately changes the mathematical Gram channel rather than diagnosing a source word.
- #5606 prepares a split helper. This supplies no helper-preparation word or invoice change.
- #5553 changes helper handoffs. This does not study or recheck those lifetimes.

The completion refresh inspected this account's open PRs created since the advance CLAIM, including #6181 and #6173. None computes the same contractive coefficient-error optimum. No additional computation was run to validate or compare predecessor results.

Live main README, merged-PR, open-PR, Discussion and local-lock searches were checked for overlap. Their coverage does not certify literature priority or unpublished work. The original three-contact CLAIM was withdrawn under the seven-day exclusion; the delivered scope follows the [explicit scope update](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19267854).
